title: A2JRAG: Process-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Public Legal Information Systems
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems ground large language model outputs in external knowledge, but they typically determine relevance through topical, semantic, or entityrelationship similarity. In process-intensive domains, such as the law, this is insufficient: information may be substantively correct yet procedurally irrelevant because it applies to a different stage of the user's matter. This paper introduces A2JRAG, a process-aware retrieval framework that conditions retrieval on an expert-authored Procedural State Graph (PSG). A PSG encodes process stages, transitions, contextual dimensions, mandatory guardrails, and escalation triggers. The evolution of RAG can be viewed in four dimensions: one-dimensional naive RAG retrieves flat facts; twodimensional relational RAG adds pairwise relationships and metadata; three-dimensional GraphRAG traverses entity-centered knowledge graphs; and four-dimensional A2JRAG adds the user's position along a temporal-procedural path. We formalize the PSG representation, describe a state-conditioned retrieval architecture, and present a planned workshop demonstration for legal self-help in North Carolina eviction proceedings. The contribution is a framework and evaluation agenda for reducing a distinct failure mode in legal AI systems: retrieval of legally accurate but procedurally mistimed and misaligned information.
